## 開篇固定收益主論點

9月2日，民間招聘轉弱，加上紐約聯準銀行總裁約翰・威廉斯對通膨情勢的評估較為溫和，暫時中斷全球債券賣壓。即使油價仍接近近期高點，美國公債仍溫和回升。2年期殖利率下降3.1個基點至4.37%，5年期下降2.1個基點至4.535%，10年期下降1.9個基點至4.78%，30年期則下滑1.6個基點至5.259%。

短端領漲，在投資人連續數個交易日上調聯準會近期升息機率後，殖利率曲線小幅呈現牛市陡峭化。2年期與10年期利差擴大1.2個基點至41個基點，2年期與30年期利差則擴大1.5個基點至88.9個基點。這波走勢稍微修復週二的跌幅，但本週殖利率仍大幅走高：2年期上升15.9個基點，5年期上升17.2個基點，10年期上升13.2個基點。

8月民間就業僅增加3.8萬人，低於市場共識的4.7萬人，也較7月的4.6萬人放緩。不過，疲弱情形集中於部分領域，不能直接解讀為經濟衰退。教育與醫療增加4.5萬個職位，休閒與餐旅增加1.6萬個，營建業增加1.2萬個；製造業減少1.7萬個，專業服務業減少1.6萬個。大型企業貢獻3.4萬個新增職位，員工少於50人的企業僅增加3,000個，薪資成長則維持穩定。

威廉斯隨後的說法，明確制衡了市場認為能源衝擊將迫使聯準會立即因應的假設。他表示，隨著關稅效應消退，通膨持續緩慢下降，能源成本上升也尚未廣泛傳導至服務業。威廉斯支持7月維持利率不變的決定，認為目前的政策設定能適當兼顧聯準會的雙重使命，但在9月15至16日會議前，仍須依據新公布的資料重新評估。

當日的債市漲勢並不代表高利率格局已經逆轉。10年期實質殖利率僅下降0.9個基點至2.432%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.348%。名目殖利率下跌因此同時來自兩個組成部分，並未明確否定實質利率或通膨壓力。聯準會褐皮書也顯示，經濟活動略為增強、就業小幅增加、價格漲勢溫和加速；資料中心與國防需求支撐製造業之際，消費者對價格則變得更加敏感。

油價仍是主要反向力量。WTI上漲0.4%，收在$90.58；布蘭特原油上漲0.56%至$95.18，本週分別累計上漲10.15%與8.36%。美國再度攻擊伊朗、伊朗採取報復行動，以及荷莫茲海峽航運受到威脅，使原油、歐洲天然氣與成品油價格持續處於高檔。因此，最新收盤反映的是美國勞動數據轉弱在單日走勢中壓過能源通膨，而非能源風險已經消失。

風險性資產將美國公債上漲視為緊縮暫歇，而非資金轉向避險。標普500指數上漲0.46%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.23%，半導體指數上漲0.45%；VIX下跌近7%至15.2，美元指數小跌0.07%，黃金期貨上漲1.9%至$4,430.50，美國高收益債利差則大致持平。整體市場較前一日平靜，但其他地區的政策緊縮仍在推進：紐西蘭升息、加拿大採取偏鷹派的按兵不動，澳洲經濟成長優於預期，日本官員則進一步強化9月升息預期。

## 招聘轉弱與威廉斯延緩聯準會重新定價

ADP報告削弱近期勞動市場訊號，但未顯示就業全面萎縮。8月就業增加3.8萬人，不僅低於4.7萬人的市場共識，也不及另一項5.1萬人的預測；前一個月僅增加4.6萬人，原本就已顯示動能有限。產業分布比整體數字更值得注意，因為新增職位高度集中於教育與醫療，其增幅甚至超過全體經濟的淨增人數。

其他服務業表現不一。休閒與餐旅增加1.6萬個職位，金融活動增加6,000個；專業服務業減少1.6萬個，資訊業減少4,000個，貿易、運輸與公用事業減少5,000個，自然資源與採礦業也減少5,000個。製造業減少1.7萬個職位，進一步顯示工廠產出擴張與勞動需求正在分歧。先前ISM報告同樣顯示產出仍處擴張區間，但訂單轉弱、價格維持高檔。

企業規模也凸顯招聘基礎狹窄。大型雇主創造3.4萬個職位，員工少於50人的企業僅有少量貢獻。小型企業通常更容易受到融資成本影響，也較缺乏吸收投入成本衝擊的能力，因此這項分布具有意義。不過，薪資成長保持穩定，使招聘放緩仍不足以構成立即的通膨降溫訊號。

威廉斯更著重於通膨的組成。他認為，關稅與能源價格上漲仍是最大的推動因素，服務業也持續帶來部分貢獻，但近期資料令人鼓舞。在他的評估中，關稅效應逐漸成為過去，最新一輪能源價格上漲也尚未廣泛外溢至其他服務項目。這項判斷直接削弱了「油價高於$90便足以要求9月升息」的論點。

他的政策立場仍取決於後續資料。威廉斯支持7月維持利率不變；當時有3名具投票權的成員主張升息25個基點。他表示，7月會議後的利率水準處於適當位置，但並未排除9月採取行動，因為官員仍在蒐集大量新資訊，之後必須重新評估。這項區別足以挑戰市場對自動升息的預設，卻不能解讀為他已承諾等待。

威廉斯也將近期長天期殖利率上升，與中性利率已永久提高的證據區分開來。他認為，這波走勢部分來自人工智慧投資與較強的成長預期，也承認若生產力持續大幅提升，最終可能推高中性利率；但目前還沒有這方面的證據。他估計中性實質利率接近1%。這套論述意味聯準會可以承認資本支出轉強，卻不必把每一次債券殖利率上升都視為均衡政策利率結構性提高的反映。

褐皮書使ADP傳達的偏弱訊息更為複雜。截至8月24日的兩個月內，經濟活動溫和增加、就業小幅上升，前景仍屬正面；但能源成本與地緣政治不確定性，使各產業的信心有所差異。國防與資料中心訂單支撐多數地區的製造業擴張，高收入消費者支出也保持穩健。

勞動需求分布不均，與民間就業報告的細節大致一致。製造、營建與部分服務業回報需求健康，零售與餐旅業則出現下降。紐約地區表示AI工程師難以招募，但初階科技與行政職位的需求轉弱。里奇蒙地區的受訪企業則指出，資料中心建設加劇搶人大戰；其中一家馬里蘭州營建公司為留住員工，將薪資提高35%。

多數地區的價格漲勢溫和加速。部分企業仍具定價能力，例如航空公司在航空燃油成本上升後維持較高票價；另一些企業則因家庭抗拒漲價而無法充分轉嫁成本。克里夫蘭地區的消費支出連續第4期下降，燃料與食品成本對家庭預算形成壓力。亞特蘭大企業表示，消費者持續轉向較便宜的產品，單次餐廳消費也下降。堪薩斯城地區則指出，汽油價格上升對中低收入與鄉村家庭造成的壓力尤其明顯。

這些證據既不符合需求全面崩落，也不表示經濟不受價格上漲影響。資料中心與國防支出正在支撐產出、部分勞動市場與資本支出；另一方面，燃料與食品成本則迫使其他領域的消費者提高價格敏感度。聯準會必須判斷，前一條傳導管道是否讓經濟活動與薪資保持足夠韌性，使能源成本得以擴散；或後一條管道會在更廣泛的通膨形成前先壓抑需求。

主席凱文・沃許既有的政策框架，使這項判斷仍有相當高的門檻。他在傑克森霍爾演說中列出的指標包括資本支出、利潤率、信用條件、消費需求、勞動利用程度與通膨廣度。一項細項統計顯示，個人消費支出籃子199個組成項目中，有54%在過去一年上漲超過3%；雖低於疫情後接近77%的高峰，仍遠高於此前20年間約32%的水準。威廉斯強調改善幅度，沃許的框架則凸顯目前分布距離先前常態仍有多遠。

美國公債收盤反映這項尚未解決的分歧。殖利率全線下降，但相較前一週的升幅，回落幅度有限。2年期殖利率為4.37%，仍足以使9月政策決定保有懸念；10年期殖利率為4.78%，也繼續包含可觀的實質利率補償。隨著債市上漲，現券交易活動降溫：FINRA記錄的美國公債面額交易量為$1.085兆，較前一日減少14%；其中名目附息債為$8,161億，下降21.3%。這些數字反映的是成交量，而非投資人方向，但顯示此次回升的交易活動低於先前的賣壓階段。

## 各國央行依不同證據收緊政策

紐西蘭採取最明確的實際緊縮行動，連續第2次會議將官方現金利率提高25個基點至2.75%。紐西蘭央行仍認為年底前可能再升息一次，但降低了儘快把利率推升至3%或更高中性水準的迫切性。總裁Anna Breman表示再次升息的可能性很高，但官員正評估前兩次行動的影響，下一次升息時點仍有高度不確定性。

市場回應的是附帶條件的前瞻指引，而非升息本身。紐西蘭元一度下跌1%，對政策敏感的2年期公債殖利率下降7個基點至3.58%。市場估計10月升息機率由會議前的65%降至約36%，12月前升息則仍接近完全反映。新預測顯示，第4季平均現金利率為2.81%，略低於5月預估的2.84%，到2027年年中則為3.07%。

通膨仍高於紐西蘭央行1%至3%的目標區間。第2季整體通膨率達4.1%，部分由燃料與其他原物料帶動；央行也將第3季預測由3.3%上調至3.9%。目前預計通膨要到2028年初才會回到2%的目標中點，晚於原先預估的2027年第3季。不過，核心通膨維持在2.7%，長期通膨預期也保持在2%附近，使央行在連續兩次升息後，得以放慢未來可能的緊縮步調。

澳洲雖未作出政策決定，市場卻進一步轉向緊縮預期。第2季GDP較前季成長0.4%，高於0.3%的預測；年增率為2.1%，也高於1.8%的市場共識與澳洲央行1.9%的估計。近6個月的成長主要來自消費支出與民間需求。

對政策敏感的3年期殖利率一度上升11個基點至4.83%，創3月以來新高。市場已反映澳洲央行最晚11月升息，並認為9月採取行動的機率超過一半；明年第1季再次升息的機率則由62%升至約80%。澳洲央行在2月至5月升息3次後，8月將現金利率維持在4.35%。

第2季GDP數據強化一項判斷：經濟活動放緩得還不夠快，無法讓通膨持續回到澳洲央行2%至3%目標區間的中點。但成長組成也有需要保留之處。一項評估指出，部分強勢來自分布不均的資料中心投資、氣旋過後礦產出口反彈，以及家庭對燃料價格上漲的反應，因此基礎成長並沒有表面數據那麼亮眼。即便如此，這項結果仍排除澳洲央行停止升息的一項潛在理由，8月勞動報告將成為產能壓力是否減輕的更直接考驗。

加拿大選擇等待，但強調通膨風險正在上升。加拿大央行連續第7次會議將隔夜利率維持在2.25%，符合經濟學家與市場預期。總裁Tiff Macklem表示通膨仍然過高，並警告中東衝突持續愈久，能源成本擴散至其他價格的可能性就愈高。

加拿大2年期公債殖利率升破3.09%，盤中創3月以來新高，加幣也走強。央行表示，經濟與通膨走勢大致符合7月預測，但通膨上行風險已經增加，新貿易壁壘也使成長前景更不確定。整體通膨率已升至3%，為2023年以來最高；核心指標則仍接近央行2%的目標。

美加貿易爭端再起，帶來範圍較窄的價格壓力。談判破裂後，美國對數百項加拿大產品課徵50%關稅，加拿大反制關稅預定9月8日生效。Macklem表示，這些措施幅度很高，但僅涵蓋加拿大對美出口約5%，因此即使受影響企業面臨嚴重衝擊，對整體經濟活動的影響可能有限。能源仍是較廣泛的總體經濟風險。

加拿大第2季經濟折合年率成長3.3%，由投資、出口與消費帶動，也削弱近期放寬政策的理由。這項決定顯示，央行可以在維持利率不變的同時，提高支持降息所需的證據門檻。紐西蘭已升息，但容許下一次行動間隔更久；加拿大則按兵不動，卻暗示必須見到經濟條件明顯轉弱才會降息。兩者的政策回應都取決於通膨的廣度與持續性，而非整體能源價格衝擊本身。

歐洲央行9月升息的訊號則進一步增強。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel表示，市場反映下週會議升息機率超過95%，代表投資人正確理解最可能的決定。歐元區8月通膨率達3.3%；Nagel認為，依據歐洲央行6月預測，通膨接近3%而非2%目標，意味利率必須提高。

Nagel並未對9月之後的政策路徑提供明確指引。他提到油氣價格波動、金融市場不穩與高度不確定性，仍主張逐次會議作出決定。由於眼前的升息幾乎已完全反映在市場價格中，這項保留尤其重要；對債市的後續影響將取決於歐洲央行是否認為能源壓力已充分傳導至薪資與基礎物價，足以延長升息循環。

## 日本轉鷹波及日圓與企業融資

10年期日本公債殖利率升至3%後，日本央行總裁植田和男與審議委員高田創釋出新政策訊號，使9月升息更為接近。植田表示，隨著基礎通膨接近2%目標，官員將更加關注物價上行風險，並確認9月17至18日會議將進行完整的政策辯論。他認為近期數據仍大致符合日本央行7月展望，也未反駁市場已完全反映9月升息的定價。

高田的立場明顯更為鷹派。這位政策委員會中最偏鷹的成員表示，近期大約每隔6個月升息25個基點的模式並非固定不變，較大幅度或連續升息都仍是選項。他並未主張特定的50或75個基點升幅，但認為環境變化已足以要求政策保留調整升息幅度與頻率的彈性。

高田的投票紀錄與這項立場一致。在7月30至31日會議中，他主張升息25個基點至1.25%，而政策委員會最終將利率維持在約1%，高田因此投下反對票。他認為日本已進入薪資與物價反應更為靈敏的新經濟格局，通膨風險偏向上行，政策應靈活因應國內外發展。他也表示，日本央行減少公債購買並非為了配合財政政策，不過維持市場有序運作仍然重要。

日圓在紐約交易時段一度升值1.2%至每美元158.22日圓，當日開盤時約在160日圓。升值速度一度引發當局是否查詢匯率或進場干預的猜測，但市場參與者未發現官方行動的明確證據，日圓隨後回吐部分漲幅。日本在此前一個月動用創紀錄的$964億支撐日圓，使交易員對160附近的任何劇烈波動格外敏感。

就可觀察到的行情起點而言，推動日圓上漲的是政策訊號，而非匯市干預。相較日本央行其他官員近期的說法，高田對可能的升息幅度與頻率都表達得更明確；植田未反駁市場完全反映9月升息，也進一步強化這項訊息。與此同時，美國財政部長史考特・貝森特公開要求日本收緊政策，提高了日本央行讓市場失望的代價，也另行帶來其行動被視為受華府驅動、而非依循國內職責的風險。

日本債市必須同時消化貨幣政策正常化與財政供給。10年期殖利率已升至3%，30年期則接近4.155%，逼近該天期推出以來的最高水準。各部會提出創紀錄的預算要求，加上首相高市早苗的擴張性計畫，使市場關注未來發債量；同一時間，日本央行也在減少購債。

殖利率上升已開始影響企業融資決策。一項針對30家仍有日圓債券流通在外之日本非金融企業的調查，收到14家公司回覆，其中數家正考慮出售資產、提前籌資或增加外幣借款。KDDI表示可能透過處分資產降低負債，中國電力則表示，利率上升可能加快出售資產及策略性持股的速度。

受訪公司在9月1日至2028年8月31日間共有¥6.74兆債券到期。豐田與東北電力表示，未來兩年到期的日圓債若進行再融資，年度利息支出可能增加逾30%。自日本央行導入負利率的時期以來，日圓債平均發行成本已增至約10倍；即使企業整體獲利仍然強勁，也迫使公司重新檢討投資報酬門檻與融資時程。

部分發行人正轉向海外市場。日本企業今年已發行超過$1,100億的美元與歐元債券，總額居亞太地區發行人之首。將募集資金換回日圓後，海外融資成本有時可以與國內借款相當，甚至更低。這項管道提供融資彈性，但也使日本貨幣政策正常化更直接地連結全球信用供給。

眼前對全球債市最直接的考驗，是日本30年期公債標售。近期殖利率接近4%的標售取得相對強勁的投標倍數，保險業者買進超長期債券的速度也已加快。不過，在殖利率高點與財政路徑都尚未確定之際，投資人仍不願積極加碼。若標售結果疲弱，可能把日本公債殖利率推向更高區間，使其長端與美國公債的利差縮至100個基點以下，進一步提高日本資金留在國內的誘因。

## 能源壓力收緊歐洲財政空間

儘管原油在紐約收盤的漲勢相對克制，美國與伊朗最新一輪衝突升級仍延續通膨推力。美軍在3天內發動第2輪攻擊，目標包括伊朗南部沿岸的雷達系統與布雷能力；伊朗則以無人機與飛彈攻擊區域內的美軍基地。德黑蘭另指控美國攻擊一場婚禮，造成5人死亡、68人受傷；美軍表示不會以平民為攻擊目標。

這場衝突透過實體供給管道影響債市。和平時期，全球約五分之一的石油與液化天然氣運量會經過荷莫茲海峽。替代輸送管線與較不透明的航運安排避免供應完全中斷，但出口仍受限制，新一輪戰事也威脅先前讓市場趨穩的局部調適措施。

成品油使衝擊進一步放大。週三之前的3個交易日，歐洲柴油期貨每天均上漲約5%；俄羅斯煉油廠遭襲，也進一步壓縮全球燃料供給。美國汽油價格維持每加侖$4以上，柴油則接近$6。原油與燃料成本走勢分歧，意味單看原油價格可能低估運輸、消費者與企業實際承受的壓力。

歐洲還面臨額外的天然氣問題。天然氣期貨上漲3%，突破每兆瓦時€74，創今年新高，本週累計上漲11%。歐洲庫存僅達容量的65%，是自2009年開始統計以來同一季節的最低水準。冬季到來前若再發生供給中斷，歐洲因此會比美國更加脆弱。

歐洲交易時段的公債表現反映這項曝險。英國10年期公債殖利率一度上升7個基點至5.29%，創2007年以來最高；同天期德國公債殖利率上升5個基點至3.39%，創2011年以來最高，法國與義大利公債殖利率也上揚。美國有偏弱的勞動數據與威廉斯言論提供國內抵銷力量，歐洲與英國市場則欠缺同類支撐，因而落後美國公債。

英國的財政計算使這波走勢更具影響。彭博經濟研究估計，殖利率與通膨上升將使政府遵守財政規則的£236億緩衝空間縮減約£120億。相關規則要求2029年的稅收足以支應日常開支。財政大臣John Healey預定10月28日公布首份預算案，使政府更難吸收新增的償債成本或支應新的承諾。

首相Andy Burnham重申政府將遵守財政規則，但未排除增加借款或加稅。他也承諾提高國防支出，並擴大政府在供水產業的角色。因此，英國公債面臨的問題並非政府已宣布放棄財政紀律，而是尚未提出具體取捨，說明如何在大致減半的緩衝空間內兌現這些承諾。

英國30年期公債殖利率升至5.86%，為1998年以來最高；5年期房貸交換利率則已升至4.52%，創2023年11月以來新高。房貸核准件數降至兩年半低點。債券賣壓已同時波及政府預算與民間融資，若政府延後釐清10月計畫，經濟代價將進一步上升。

法國承受的是相關但不同的政治風險溢價。法國與德國10年期公債利差略低於88個基點，接近歐債危機時期的水準。Nagel否決總統候選人Jean-Luc Mélenchon提出的方案；該方案主張取消法國央行與歐洲央行持有的法國債務。Nagel表示，歐洲條約禁止貨幣融資，這類做法最終可能引發嚴重通膨。這項發言並非造成法國財政風險的原因，卻明確指出債務取消不能視為可用的資產負債表解方。

中國面對的政策組合正好相反。10年期中國公債殖利率維持在1.69%附近，美國公債則約為4.8%，使中美利差接近創紀錄的315個基點。中央與地方政府前8個月僅使用約68%的年度發債額度，低於一年前的76%，政府借款速度因此即將加快。其中中央政府債發行量僅達額度的65%，是2022年以來最慢進度。

預期中的債券供給使市場轉而關注中國人民銀行的流動性支援。8月，人行透過中期借貸便利與買斷式逆回購僅提供人民幣1,000億元資金，低於7月的人民幣8,000億元。成長疲弱與風險偏好低迷持續壓低殖利率，但財政發債加速後，央行可能需要加大資金投放，避免融資成本無序上升。

## 信用市場保持暢通，困境風險更趨個別化

美國市場轉趨平靜，高收益債利差大致持平，但個別交易與困境債權的表現仍明顯分化。Kingspan透過兩批綠色債券籌得€8.5億，最終認購需求為€31億，低於高峰時超過€46億。較短天期債券以中間交換利率加63個基點定價，較長天期則加95個基點。預期評等為BBB級，募集資金將用於合格綠色專案。

Kingspan營運前景改善也支撐認購需求。這家隔熱材料製造商將全年營業利潤預測由€10.5億上調至€11.3億，資料中心材料業務的訂單則較一年前增加逾1倍。這筆已完成的發行顯示，即使政府公債殖利率上升，與AI建設相關的高評級借款人仍能吸引數倍於發行規模的需求。

Waymo則以私募債務為同類資本支出需求籌資。Alphabet旗下自駕車事業正進行最後階段的融資洽談，擬向Pimco、Blackstone及Sixth Street等貸款機構取得超過$30億資金。這筆未評等貸款的利率可能比基準利率高逾500個基點。Waymo過去主要依賴股權融資，今年稍早便以$1,260億估值募得$160億；但AI與車隊成本上升，正促使公司擴大資本來源。

這筆債務將支應Waymo擴張，朝今年在20座城市每週提供100萬次付費乘車服務的目標前進；目前其在美國14座城市每週提供逾50萬次服務。相對基準利率的擬議溢酬，既反映成長機會，也反映這家首次借款、且持續有龐大資金需求的企業所面臨的執行風險。

Ukrenergo的重整方案更清楚區分新資金所獲保障與既有債務的回收條件。這家烏克蘭電網營運商已取得美國國際開發金融公司的擔保，將為至少$4.45億的新債券提供支持。募集資金將用於回購其$8.25億歐洲債券的一部分；該債券自2024年底以來已暫停付息。

債券持有人可以按面額的60%至65.125%出售持債，也可按1比1比例將債權交換為票息8.5%、但未獲該擔保的新債。換債所得債券將自2028年6月起分8期等額攤還，並在交割後支付一筆涵蓋2025年7月以來期間的利息。現金回購上限為$4.45億，且以DFC擔保的融資完成為前提。

這項架構並未把美國的擔保延伸至換債所得的新券。既有債權人因此必須比較折價現金回收，與對一家基礎設施持續遭受攻擊的公用事業公司所持有之較長期、未獲該擔保債權。方案也必須在10月1日的線上會議取得債券持有人批准。籌資若成功，將改善Ukrenergo取得重建融資的能力；但在這些條件滿足前，現金回購與換債都不會生效。

塞內加爾政府同意申請強化版G20共同框架下的債務處理，作為擬議$22億IMF計畫的一部分，市場因而持續反映很可能進行債務重整。以歐元計價的2028年到期債券週二一度下跌超過8分，之後收斂跌幅，賣出成交最高達$1,310萬。投資人也關注主權發行人是否會支付9月13日到期的票息。

這檔短天期債券先前的交易邏輯，是即使談判拖延，債權人仍可能收到近期款項。共同框架公告降低了這項預期，使2028年債券的價格更接近長天期債券所反映的回收水準。明年3月有一筆$5.47億的本金與利息到期，部分投資人目前預期，所有歐洲債券都會在此前重新安排條款。

週三的反彈並未重建市場信心。交易員認為行情主要來自空頭回補，部分實質資金投資人反而利用反彈降低曝險。目前仍不確定既有重整範圍是否足以恢復債務可持續性、短天期債權人是否會獲得不同選項，以及政府打算如何在不讓債權人承受損失的情況下推動債務處理。

澳洲Bathla破產則暴露另一種集中風險。這家房地產開發商曾向眾多非銀行貸款機構借款，提供的報酬率通常接近15%。澳洲私募信貸市場規模約A$2,000億，其中多達60%的放款流向房地產。營建成本上升、住宅需求下降與專案延宕，使各貸款機構面對截然不同的擔保品與完工前景。

Bathla陷入困境後，多家私募信貸公司限制贖回。Centuria Bass暫停兩項投資工具的贖回，但表示預期旗下基金不會受到重大影響。放款超過A$3億的PAG則未限制贖回，因為該公司認為其債權擔保充分，獲償機率較高。Balmain計畫再提供A$100萬，完成一項公寓工程；PAG則承諾直接向另一項312戶住宅開發案的承包商付款。

這些行動顯示，不能從同一則負面消息直接推斷基金流動性與貸款回收結果。為接近完工的建築提供融資時，貸款機構可能透過有限的追加資金保存價值；若債權只以土地或初期工程為擔保，則可能需要更換開發商並投入更多資金。據報Bathla已質押超過A$45億的土地、房地產與房貸款項，但實際可回收價值取決於特定資產、施工階段與債權順位。

土耳其龐大的利差交易部位則帶來另一種流動性風險。在37%的政策利率吸引下，外國投資人估計已將$750億投入高收益里拉衍生品與貨幣市場基金，其中約$100億在里拉基金，$650億在外匯遠期。資金流入支撐了外匯存底與里拉，但部位天期短，一旦再度發生地緣政治衝擊，政策制定者便可能面臨資金迅速逆轉。

官員正考慮對貨幣市場基金收益課稅，以抑制不穩定的資金流入。不過，這項措施也可能削弱國內儲蓄者持有里拉的誘因，尤其是在央行開始降息的情況下。銀行融資利率已由40%的緊急利率回落至37%的主要政策利率，市場因而重新預期9月可能降息。政策難題在於，既要降低對短期利差交易的依賴，又不能削弱支撐通膨降溫與外匯存底重建的力量。

## 前瞻市場意涵

9月2日收盤顯示，即使油價接近$95，美國公債仍會因招聘轉弱而上漲，因此接下來的勞動與服務業數據權重提高。首次申領失業救濟金人數將於9月3日紐約時間上午8時30分公布，預期為20.5萬人，前值20.3萬人。截至8月22日當週的持續申領人數，將檢驗失業是否變得更持久；前值為177.8萬人。

同日上午8時30分還將公布7月貿易數據與第2季生產力終值。貿易逆差預計由$733億擴大至$900億；非農生產力增幅預計由0.8%上修至1.4%，單位勞動成本增幅則預計維持在1.3%。生產力估值若轉強，將支持AI投資具有供給面效益的解讀，但單憑這項資料仍不足以證明威廉斯所說的中性利率上升條件已經成立。

標普全球服務業PMI終值將在上午9時45分公布，預期由54.6升至56.8；ISM服務業指數則在上午10時公布，預測由54.1升至54.3。價格、就業與新業務分項將決定製造業所呈現的組合——經濟活動有韌性、招聘轉弱、成本維持高檔——是否正在擴散至規模更大的服務業。

9月4日上午8時30分公布的8月就業報告，仍是聯準會會前最關鍵的勞動市場考驗。市場共識預期非農就業增加5.8萬人，前值為減少2.3萬人；失業率預計維持在4.1%，平均時薪月增率則由0.1%加速至0.3%。相較ADP估計的3.8萬人，官方招聘的產業廣度、數據修正、失業率與薪資更為重要。若招聘疲弱擴散至更多產業，且薪資壓力未再升高，威廉斯主張耐心等待的理由將增強；若薪資與勞動利用程度保持穩健，沃許的通膨判準仍會主導政策討論。

日本30年期公債標售是眼前最重要的全球債市事件。該天期殖利率約4.155%，先前殖利率接近4%的標售取得相對強勁的投標倍數，保險業者買盤也已增加。然而，高田願意考慮更大幅度或連續升息，提高了投資人要求進一步發行讓利的風險。若標售需求疲弱，日本公債殖利率可能進一步上升，相對美國公債的吸引力也會增強。

Nagel認同市場的升息定價後，歐洲央行9月10日的決定已大致在預期之中。9月之後的政策指引將決定這次行動只是對3.3%通膨率的有限回應，或是一段更持久緊縮階段的起點。關鍵區別在於能源成本是否傳導至服務價格與薪資，而非原油是否再次上漲。

聯準會將於9月15至16日開會，目前訊號仍相互矛盾。ADP招聘轉弱、威廉斯認為關稅效應正在消退，美國公債殖利率當日也有所下降；相對地，褐皮書顯示價格漲勢溫和加快，原油與成品油仍處高檔，沃許也強調通膨廣度仍遠高於疫情前常態。就業、服務業通膨與之後的生產者物價報告，必須決定單日的美國公債漲勢能否演變為持續性的政策重新評估。

日本央行將於9月17至18日接續召開會議，市場已完全反映升息25個基點。植田最新談話支持採取行動，高田則把討論擴大至升息幅度與後續行動頻率。政策聲明因此必須處理9月之後的路徑，才足以明顯改變市場預期。若只是例行升息而未提供指引，日圓可能重新轉弱；更強硬的訊號則會加重已傳導至日本公債標售與企業資產負債表的融資壓力。

信用市場結果取決於交易與方案能否完成，而非只有基準利率方向。塞內加爾必須釐清9月13日票息與擬議債務處理的範圍；Ukrenergo必須完成DFC擔保的籌資，並在10月1日取得債權人同意；Bathla的貸款機構則須判斷哪些專案值得追加完工資金、哪些擔保品足以支撐回收。在每個案例中，美國公債溫和上漲只能略微改變折現率，無法解決真正決定債權人價值的順位、擔保、流動性與現金流問題。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries recovered modestly on Sept. 2 as weaker private hiring and a less alarmed inflation assessment from New York Fed President John Williams interrupted the global duration selloff, even while oil remained near its latest highs. The 2-year yield declined 3.1 basis points to 4.37%, the 5-year fell 2.1 basis points to 4.535%, the 10-year eased 1.9 basis points to 4.78% and the 30-year slipped 1.6 basis points to 5.259%.

The front end led the rally, producing a small bull steepening after several sessions in which investors had marked up the likelihood of near-term Fed tightening. The 2s10s spread widened 1.2 basis points to 41 basis points, while 2s30s increased 1.5 basis points to 88.9. The move offered some relief from Tuesday’s selloff but left yields substantially higher over the week: the 2-year was up 15.9 basis points, the 5-year 17.2 and the 10-year 13.2.

August private payrolls increased by only 38,000, missing the 47,000 consensus and slowing from 46,000 in July. The weakness was concentrated enough to resist a simple recessionary reading. Education and health added 45,000 jobs, leisure and hospitality 16,000 and construction 12,000, while manufacturing lost 17,000 and professional services shed 16,000. Large companies accounted for 34,000 of the increase, firms with fewer than 50 employees added just 3,000 and pay growth was steady.

Williams then supplied an explicit counterweight to the market’s assumption that the energy shock would force an immediate Fed response. He said inflation had continued to trend slowly lower as tariff effects faded and that higher energy costs had not spread broadly into services. Williams, who supported the July decision to hold rates steady, described the current setting as well placed to balance the Fed’s mandates, while preserving the need to reassess the incoming data before the Sept. 15-16 meeting.

The day’s rally did not amount to an unwind of the higher-rate regime. The 10-year real yield declined only 0.9 basis point to 2.432%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 1 basis point to 2.348%. Both components therefore contributed to the nominal move, rather than the session producing a decisive rejection of either real-rate or inflation pressure. The Fed’s Beige Book also described modestly stronger activity, slightly higher employment and moderately accelerating prices, with data-center and defense demand supporting manufacturing even as consumers became more price-sensitive.

Oil remained the principal counterforce. WTI finished 0.4% higher at $90.58 and Brent gained 0.56% to $95.18, leaving them up 10.15% and 8.36%, respectively, over the week. Renewed US strikes against Iran, Iranian retaliation and threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz kept crude, European gas and refined fuels elevated. The latest close therefore showed softer US labor evidence winning a daily contest against energy inflation, not the disappearance of the energy risk.

Risk markets treated the Treasury rally as a pause in tightening rather than a flight to safety. The S&P 500 rose 0.46%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.23% and the semiconductor index increased 0.45%. The VIX fell almost 7% to 15.2, the Dollar Index edged 0.07% lower and gold futures rose 1.9% to $4,430.50. US high-yield spreads were little changed. That combination left the session calmer than the previous one, even as policy tightening advanced elsewhere: New Zealand raised rates, Canada delivered a hawkish hold, Australian growth beat forecasts, and Japanese officials reinforced expectations of a September increase.

## Softer Hiring and Williams Slow the Fed Repricing

The ADP report weakened the near-term labor signal without showing a uniformly contracting jobs market. Its 38,000 increase undershot both the 47,000 consensus and the 51,000 separate forecast, while the previous month’s 46,000 gain had already indicated limited momentum. The industry split was more consequential than the headline alone because the additions depended heavily on education and health, which created more jobs than the economy-wide net increase.

Other service categories were mixed. Leisure and hospitality added 16,000 positions and financial activities gained 6,000, but professional services lost 16,000, information declined by 4,000, and trade, transportation and utilities shed 5,000. Natural resources and mining also lost 5,000. Manufacturing’s 17,000 decline broadened the evidence that factory expansion and labor demand were moving differently, following the earlier ISM report in which output remained in expansion while orders softened and prices stayed elevated.

Company size added another sign of narrowness. Large employers generated 34,000 jobs, leaving only a small contribution from businesses with fewer than 50 workers. That distribution matters because smaller firms are often more exposed to financing costs and have less capacity to absorb input-price shocks. Stable pay growth nevertheless limited the case for treating the hiring slowdown as an immediate disinflation signal.

Williams focused instead on the composition of inflation. He said tariffs and higher energy prices remained its largest drivers, with some continuing contribution from services, but judged the recent data encouraging. In his assessment, tariff effects were increasingly moving into the past, while the latest energy increase had not yet produced a broad spillover into other services. That directly qualified the argument that oil above $90 by itself required a September increase.

His policy position remained conditional. Williams backed the July hold, when three voting members dissented in favor of a 25-basis-point increase, and said rates were in a good place after that meeting. He did not rule out action in September; he said officials were collecting substantial new information and would need to reassess. The distinction was enough to challenge the presumption of an automatic increase without turning his remarks into a promise to wait.

Williams also separated the current rise in longer-term yields from evidence that the economy’s neutral rate had permanently increased. He attributed part of the move to artificial-intelligence investment and expectations of stronger growth, and acknowledged that a sustained productivity boom could eventually lift the neutral rate. He said the evidence was not there yet and put his own estimate of the neutral real rate near 1%. The argument leaves the Fed able to recognize stronger capital expenditure without assuming that every increase in bond yields reflects a structurally higher equilibrium policy rate.

The Beige Book complicated the softer message from ADP. Economic activity increased modestly over the two months through Aug. 24, employment rose slightly and the outlook was positive, although sentiment differed across sectors because of energy costs and geopolitical uncertainty. Manufacturing expanded in most districts, supported by defense and data-center orders, while high-end consumer spending remained solid.

Labor demand was uneven in a way that broadly matched the private-payroll details. Manufacturing, construction and some services reported healthy demand, but retail and hospitality showed declines. The New York district described AI engineers as difficult to find while demand for entry-level technology and administrative roles weakened. Richmond contacts reported that data-center construction had intensified competition for workers, including a Maryland construction company that raised pay 35% to retain staff.

Prices accelerated moderately in most districts. Some businesses retained pricing power, including airlines that maintained higher fares after jet-fuel costs rose. Others found that household resistance limited pass-through. Cleveland reported a fourth consecutive period of declining consumer spending as fuel and food costs strained budgets, while Atlanta businesses described a continued shift toward cheaper products and lower restaurant spending per visit. Kansas City contacts said higher gasoline costs were creating particular stress for low- and moderate-income and rural households.

That evidence fits neither a broad demand collapse nor an economy immune to higher prices. Data-center and defense spending are supporting output, selected labor markets and capital expenditure, while fuel and food costs are forcing more price-sensitive behavior elsewhere. For the Fed, the issue is whether the first channel keeps activity and wages firm enough for energy costs to spread, or whether the second constrains demand before broader inflation develops.

Chair Kevin Warsh’s existing framework keeps that test demanding. The data indicators highlighted in his Jackson Hole address include capital expenditure, profit margins, credit conditions, consumer demand, labor utilization and the breadth of inflation. One detailed measure showed that 54% of the 199 components in the personal consumption expenditures basket had risen more than 3% over the past year, down from a post-pandemic peak near 77% but still well above the roughly 32% share that prevailed during the preceding two decades. Williams’s remarks emphasized the improvement; Warsh’s framework emphasizes how far the distribution remains from its earlier norm.

The Treasury close reflected that unresolved difference. Yields declined across the curve, but the move was small relative to the preceding week’s increase. At 4.37%, the 2-year yield remained high enough to keep the September decision live, while the 10-year at 4.78% continued to embed substantial real-rate compensation. Cash activity moderated as the rally developed: FINRA recorded $1.085 trillion of Treasury par traded, 14% less than the previous day, including $816.1 billion of nominal coupons, down 21.3%. Those figures describe turnover rather than investor direction, but they show that the retracement occurred with less activity than the preceding selloff.

## Central Banks Tighten on Different Evidence

New Zealand delivered the clearest realized tightening step, raising the Official Cash Rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% for a second consecutive meeting. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand retained the likelihood of one more increase by year-end but reduced the urgency around reaching a neutral setting of 3% or more. Governor Anna Breman said another increase was likely, while stressing that its timing was highly uncertain as officials assessed the effects of the two moves already delivered.

Markets responded to the conditional guidance rather than the rate increase itself. The New Zealand dollar fell as much as 1%, and the policy-sensitive 2-year government yield declined 7 basis points to 3.58%. The probability of an October increase dropped to about 36% from 65% before the meeting, while an increase by December remained just short of fully priced. The new forecast put the average cash rate at 2.81% in Q4, slightly below the 2.84% projected in May, and at 3.07% by mid-2027.

Inflation remains above the RBNZ’s 1%-to-3% target range. Headline inflation reached 4.1% in Q2, driven in part by fuel and other materials, and the bank raised its Q3 forecast to 3.9% from 3.3%. It now expects inflation to return to the 2% target midpoint in early 2028 rather than Q3 2027. Core inflation held at 2.7%, however, and longer-term expectations remained near 2%, allowing the bank to slow the prospective cadence after two back-to-back increases.

Australia moved toward tighter expectations without a policy decision. Q2 GDP grew 0.4% from the previous quarter, beating the 0.3% forecast, and expanded 2.1% from a year earlier, above both the 1.8% consensus and the Reserve Bank of Australia’s 1.9% estimate. Consumer spending and private demand contributed most of the growth over the latest six months.

The policy-sensitive 3-year yield rose as much as 11 basis points to 4.83%, its highest since March, while markets priced an RBA increase by November and treated September as more likely than not. The probability of another move in Q1 next year rose to about 80% from 62%. The RBA had kept its cash rate at 4.35% in August after raising it three times between February and May.

The headline GDP result strengthens the case that activity is not slowing fast enough to return inflation sustainably to the midpoint of the RBA’s 2%-to-3% range. Its composition carries qualifications. One assessment attributed part of the strength to uneven data-center investment, a rebound in mining exports after cyclones and households’ response to higher fuel prices, arguing that underlying growth was less impressive. The result nevertheless removed one potential reason for the RBA to stop, leaving the August labor report as a more direct test of whether capacity pressure is easing.

Canada chose to wait but emphasized a growing inflation risk. The Bank of Canada held its overnight rate at 2.25% for a seventh consecutive meeting, matching economist and market expectations. Governor Tiff Macklem said inflation was too high and warned that the longer the Middle East conflict persisted, the greater the chance that energy costs would spread into other prices.

Canadian 2-year yields rose above 3.09%, their highest intraday level since March, and the Canadian dollar strengthened. The bank said the economy and inflation were evolving broadly in line with its July projections, but that upside inflation risks had increased while new trade barriers made the growth outlook less certain. Headline inflation had reached 3%, its highest since 2023, although core measures remained near the bank’s 2% objective.

The renewed US-Canada trade dispute added a narrower source of price pressure. The US imposed 50% duties on hundreds of Canadian products after negotiations failed, and Canadian counter-tariffs are scheduled to start Sept. 8. Macklem said the measures were steep but covered about 5% of exports to the US, limiting their likely effect on aggregate activity even as affected companies face a severe shock. Energy remained the larger economy-wide concern.

The Canadian economy’s 3.3% annualized Q2 rebound, driven by investment, exports and consumption, also reduced the case for near-term relief. The decision showed how a central bank can hold rates while shifting the burden of proof against easing. New Zealand delivered a hike but allowed more time before another; Canada stayed put but signaled that cuts would require materially weaker conditions. Both responses turned on the breadth and persistence of inflation rather than the headline energy shock alone.

The European Central Bank’s September move became still more strongly signaled. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said market pricing of more than a 95% probability of an increase at next week’s meeting reflected a sound understanding of the likely decision. Euro-area inflation reached 3.3% in August, and Nagel argued that inflation near 3%, rather than the 2% target, required higher rates under the ECB’s June projections.

Nagel stopped short of guiding the path beyond September. He cited volatile oil and gas prices, unsettled financial markets and substantial uncertainty, retaining a meeting-by-meeting approach. That caution matters because the immediate increase is almost fully discounted; the duration consequence depends on whether the ECB sees energy pressure spreading into wages and underlying prices strongly enough to extend the cycle.

## Japan’s Hawkish Shift Reaches the Yen and Corporate Funding

The Bank of Japan moved closer to a September increase as Governor Kazuo Ueda and board member Hajime Takata added new policy signals after the 10-year JGB yield reached 3%. Ueda said officials would give greater attention to upside price risks as underlying inflation approached the 2% target and confirmed that the Sept. 17-18 meeting would include a full policy debate. He said recent data remained broadly consistent with the BOJ’s July outlook and did not push back against a market that had fully priced a September move.

Takata went materially further. The board’s most hawkish member said the recent pattern of 25-basis-point increases roughly six months apart was not fixed and left open both a larger move and back-to-back hikes. He did not advocate a specific 50- or 75-basis-point increase, but said the environment had changed enough that the size and frequency of tightening should remain flexible.

His position carries a clear voting record. Takata dissented at the July 30-31 meeting in favor of raising the policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, while the board held it around 1%. He argued that Japan had entered a new economic regime in which wages and prices were more responsive, inflation risks were tilted upward and policy should adjust nimbly to domestic and overseas developments. He also said the BOJ’s reduction in government-bond purchases was not intended to accommodate fiscal policy, although maintaining orderly market function remained important.

The yen rallied as much as 1.2% to 158.22 per dollar during New York trading after beginning the day near 160. The speed of the move briefly prompted speculation that authorities might be checking exchange rates or intervening, but market participants found no clear evidence of official action. The currency subsequently pared part of the gain. Japan had spent a record $96.4 billion supporting the yen during the preceding month, leaving traders unusually sensitive to any sharp move around 160.

The policy signal, rather than intervention, provided the observable starting point for the rally. Takata’s remarks were more explicit than recent comments from other BOJ officials on both the possible size and cadence of increases. Ueda’s refusal to resist fully priced September expectations reinforced the message. At the same time, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s public pressure for tighter Japanese policy has increased the cost of disappointing the market and created a separate risk that BOJ action appears driven by Washington rather than its domestic mandate.

Japan’s bond market must absorb monetary normalization alongside fiscal supply. The 10-year yield had already reached 3%, and the 30-year stood near 4.155%, close to its highest level since that tenor was introduced. Record ministry budget requests and Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s expansionary plans have focused attention on future issuance, while the BOJ is reducing purchases.

Higher yields are now reaching corporate financing decisions. A survey of 30 Japanese nonfinancial companies with yen bonds outstanding received responses from 14, several of which were considering asset sales, earlier funding or additional foreign-currency borrowing. KDDI said it could use asset disposals to reduce debt, while Chugoku Electric Power said higher rates could accelerate the sale of assets and strategic shareholdings.

The companies surveyed have ¥6.74 trillion of bonds maturing between Sept. 1 and Aug. 31, 2028. Toyota and Tohoku Electric said refinancing their yen notes due during the next two years could raise annual interest expense by more than 30%. The average cost of issuing yen bonds has increased roughly tenfold from the era when the BOJ introduced negative rates, forcing companies to reconsider hurdle rates and financing calendars even though aggregate corporate profits remain strong.

Some issuers are moving offshore. Japanese companies have sold more than $110 billion of dollar- and euro-denominated bonds this year, the largest total among Asia-Pacific issuers. Foreign funding can sometimes be obtained at costs comparable with or below domestic borrowing after proceeds are swapped into yen. That channel provides flexibility, but it also connects Japan’s normalization more directly to global credit supply.

The immediate duration test is Japan’s 30-year auction. Recent sales near a 4% yield achieved relatively strong bid-to-cover ratios, and insurer purchases of super-long bonds have accelerated. Investors nevertheless remain reluctant to add aggressively while neither the peak in yields nor the fiscal path is settled. A weak sale would risk pushing JGBs into a higher range and narrowing the long-end yield gap with Treasuries below 100 basis points, strengthening the incentive for Japanese capital to remain at home.

## Energy Pressure Tightens Europe’s Fiscal Constraint

The latest US-Iran escalation kept the inflationary impulse alive even though crude’s New York close was relatively contained. US forces carried out a second round of attacks in three days, targeting radar systems and mine-laying capabilities along Iran’s southern coast. Iran responded with drone and missile attacks on US bases around the region. Tehran also accused the US of striking a wedding ceremony, killing five people and injuring 68; the US military said it does not target civilians.

The conflict matters to bonds through the physical supply channel. Roughly one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied-gas flows passed through the Strait of Hormuz during peacetime. Workaround pipelines and less visible shipping have prevented a complete halt, but exports remain constrained, and the renewed fighting threatens the partial adaptation that had stabilized markets.

Refined products are amplifying the shock. European diesel futures rose about 5% in each of the three sessions before Wednesday, while attacks on Russian refineries further restricted global fuel supply. US gasoline remained above $4 a gallon and diesel approached $6. The divergence between crude and fuel costs means headline oil alone may understate the pressure reaching transport, consumers and businesses.

Europe faces an additional natural-gas problem. Gas futures rose 3% to more than €74 per megawatt-hour, their highest level of the year, and were up 11% for the week. European inventories were only 65% full, the lowest seasonal level in records dating to 2009. That combination left the region more sensitive than the US to another disruption ahead of winter.

Government bonds reflected that exposure during the European session. The 10-year gilt yield rose as much as 7 basis points to 5.29%, its highest since 2007, while the comparable German yield gained 5 basis points to 3.39%, its highest since 2011. French and Italian yields also rose. Europe and the UK underperformed Treasuries as softer US labor data and Williams provided a domestic offset that their markets lacked.

Britain’s fiscal arithmetic made the move more consequential. Bloomberg Economics estimated that higher yields and inflation would reduce the government’s £23.6 billion buffer against its fiscal rules by about £12 billion. Those rules require tax revenue to cover day-to-day spending in 2029. Chancellor John Healey is due to present his first budget on Oct. 28, leaving less room to absorb higher debt-service costs or new commitments.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham reaffirmed that his government would follow the fiscal rules but declined to rule out either additional borrowing or tax increases. He has also promised higher defense spending and a greater public role in the water industry. The issue for gilts is therefore not a declared abandonment of fiscal discipline, but the absence of detailed choices showing how those commitments fit within a buffer that has roughly halved.

The 30-year gilt yield reached 5.86%, a level last seen in 1998, while 5-year mortgage swaps had climbed to 4.52%, their highest since November 2023. Mortgage approvals fell to their lowest in two and a half years. The bond selloff is thus reaching both the budget and private financing, increasing the economic cost of any delay in clarifying the October plan.

France carries a related but distinct political premium. The spread between 10-year French debt and German bunds was just under 88 basis points, near levels last seen around the sovereign-debt crisis. Nagel rejected a proposal by presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon to cancel French debt held by the Bank of France and ECB, saying monetary financing was prohibited under European treaties and could ultimately produce severe inflation. The statement did not create France’s fiscal risk, but it clarified that debt cancellation cannot be treated as an available balance-sheet solution.

China faces the opposite policy configuration. Its 10-year yield held near 1.69% while Treasuries traded around 4.8%, taking the US-China gap close to a record 315 basis points. Government borrowing is set to accelerate because central and local authorities used only about 68% of their annual bond quota in the first eight months, compared with 76% a year earlier. Sovereign issuance alone reached just 65% of quota, the slowest pace since 2022.

The prospective supply puts attention on People’s Bank of China liquidity support. The central bank provided only 100 billion yuan through its medium-term lending facility and outright reverse repos in August, down from 800 billion yuan in July. Weak growth and risk appetite continue to suppress yields, but faster fiscal issuance could require larger injections to prevent a disorderly increase in funding costs.

## Credit Markets Stay Open as Distress Becomes More Specific

The calmer US session left high-yield spreads little changed, but individual transactions and distressed credits continued to diverge sharply. Kingspan raised €850 million through a two-part green-bond sale after receiving €3.1 billion of final demand, down from a peak above €4.6 billion. The shorter tranche priced 63 basis points over mid-swaps and the longer tranche at 95 basis points. The expected BBB-rated proceeds are earmarked for eligible green projects.

Demand benefited from Kingspan’s improving operating outlook. The insulation producer raised its full-year trading-profit forecast to €1.13 billion from €1.05 billion, while orders at its data-center-materials business more than doubled from a year earlier. The completed sale showed that high-grade borrowers linked to the AI buildout could still attract several times the offered amount despite the rise in government yields.

Waymo approached the same capital theme through private debt. Alphabet’s autonomous-driving unit was in final talks for more than $3 billion from lenders including Pimco, Blackstone and Sixth Street. The unrated loan could price more than 500 basis points over its benchmark. Waymo has traditionally relied on equity, including a $16 billion raising earlier this year at a $126 billion valuation, but rising AI and fleet costs are pushing it toward a broader capital structure.

The debt would finance expansion toward Waymo’s goal of 1 million paid weekly rides across 20 cities this year, from more than 500,000 trips in 14 US cities. The proposed premium over benchmark rates reflects both the growth opportunity and the execution risk of lending to a first-time borrower with large continuing capital needs.

Ukrenergo’s restructuring presented a sharper distinction between new-money protection and recoveries on existing debt. Ukraine’s power-grid operator secured a guarantee from the US International Development Finance Corporation for at least $445 million of new bonds. The proceeds would finance a buyback of part of its $825 million Eurobond, on which interest has been suspended since late 2024.

Bondholders may tender for 60% to 65.125% of face value or exchange their claims 1:1 into new unguaranteed debt paying 8.5%. The exchange bonds would amortize in eight equal installments beginning in June 2028 and make an interest payment after settlement covering the period from July 2025. The cash buyback is capped at $445 million and depends on the DFC-backed financing being completed.

The structure does not extend the US guarantee to the exchange notes. Existing creditors must therefore compare discounted cash recovery with a longer, unguaranteed claim on a utility whose infrastructure continues to face attack. The plan also requires bondholder approval at an Oct. 1 virtual meeting. Successful fundraising would improve Ukrenergo’s access to reconstruction finance, but neither leg becomes effective before those conditions are met.

Senegal’s market continued to price a likely restructuring after the government agreed to seek a debt treatment under an enhanced version of the G20 Common Framework as part of a proposed $2.2 billion IMF program. The euro-denominated 2028 bond fell more than 8 cents on Tuesday before paring the decline, while sales reached as much as $13.1 million. Investors also focused on whether the sovereign would make a coupon payment due Sept. 13.

The short maturity had previously traded on the possibility that creditors could receive near-term payments while negotiations dragged on. The Common Framework announcement reduced that expectation and pulled the 2028 bond closer to the recovery pricing of longer maturities. A $547 million principal-and-interest payment is due in March, and some investors now expect all eurobonds to be reworked before then.

Wednesday’s rebound did not establish renewed confidence. Traders attributed the move largely to short covering, and some real-money investors used it to reduce exposure. Uncertainty remains over whether the current restructuring perimeter is wide enough to restore debt sustainability, whether short-dated creditors receive a different menu and how the government intends to pursue a treatment without creditor losses.

Australia’s Bathla insolvency exposed another form of concentration risk. The property developer had borrowed from a wide group of non-bank lenders, often offering returns near 15%, in a private-credit market of about A$200 billion where as much as 60% of lending has gone to real estate. Higher construction costs, falling housing demand and delayed projects have left lenders with sharply different collateral and completion prospects.

Several private-credit firms capped withdrawals after Bathla’s distress. Centuria Bass halted redemptions in two vehicles while saying it did not expect a material effect on its funds. PAG, which lent more than A$300 million, did not restrict withdrawals because it considers its position well secured and more likely to be repaid. Balmain planned to advance another A$1 million to finish an apartment project, while PAG committed to pay contractors directly on a separate 312-unit development.

Those actions show why fund liquidity and loan recovery cannot be inferred from the same headline. A lender financing a nearly completed building may preserve value by supplying limited additional capital; a claim against land or an early-stage project may require a new developer and more extensive funding. Bathla reportedly pledged more than A$4.5 billion of land, property and mortgage payments as collateral, but the recoverable value depends on the specific asset, construction stage and claim priority.

Turkey’s large carry position creates a different liquidity risk. Foreign investors have placed an estimated $75 billion into high-yielding lira derivatives and money-market funds, attracted by the 37% policy rate. About $10 billion is estimated to be in lira funds and $65 billion in currency forwards. The inflows have supported reserves and the currency, but their short maturity leaves policymakers exposed to rapid reversal during another geopolitical shock.

Officials are considering a tax on money-market-fund returns to discourage unstable flows. That measure could also weaken the incentive for domestic savers to remain in lira, especially if the central bank begins cutting rates. Markets have revived expectations of a September reduction after bank funding shifted from a 40% emergency rate back to the main 37% rate. The policy challenge is to reduce reliance on short-term carry without removing one of the supports for disinflation and reserve rebuilding.

## Forward Market Significance

US labor and services data now carry more weight because the Sept. 2 close showed Treasuries responding to softer hiring even with oil near $95. Initial jobless claims are due Sept. 3 at 8:30 a.m. New York time, with 205,000 expected after 203,000. Continuing claims for the week through Aug. 22 will test whether unemployment is becoming more persistent; the prior reading was 1.778 million.

The same 8:30 release window includes July trade and final Q2 productivity data. The trade deficit is expected to widen to $90 billion from $73.3 billion. Nonfarm productivity is expected to be revised to 1.4% from 0.8%, while unit labor-cost growth is expected to remain at 1.3%. A stronger productivity estimate would support the supply-side interpretation of AI investment, but it would not by itself establish Williams’s higher neutral-rate condition.

The final S&P Global services PMI follows at 9:45 a.m., with 56.8 expected after 54.6, and ISM services is due at 10 a.m., forecast at 54.3 after 54.1. The prices, employment and new-business details will determine whether the combination seen in manufacturing—resilient activity, softer hiring and elevated costs—is spreading through the larger services sector.

August payrolls remain the central pre-Fed labor test on Sept. 4 at 8:30 a.m. Consensus calls for a 58,000 increase after a 23,000 decline, with unemployment holding at 4.1% and monthly average hourly earnings accelerating to 0.3% from 0.1%. The comparison with ADP’s 38,000 estimate will matter less than the breadth of official hiring, revisions, unemployment and wages. Williams’s case for patience becomes stronger if weak hiring extends beyond a few industries without renewed pay pressure; Warsh’s inflation standard remains dominant if wages and labor utilization stay firm.

Japan’s 30-year auction is the immediate global-duration event. The tenor yields about 4.155%, previous auctions near 4% attracted relatively strong coverage and insurer buying has increased. Takata’s willingness to consider larger or consecutive hikes, however, has raised the risk that investors demand still more concession. A weak auction could push Japanese yields higher and strengthen the relative appeal of domestic bonds over Treasuries.

The ECB’s Sept. 10 decision is largely anticipated after Nagel endorsed market pricing of a hike. Guidance beyond September will determine whether the move is a limited response to inflation at 3.3% or the start of a more persistent tightening phase. Energy pass-through into services and wages, rather than another rise in crude alone, is the critical distinction.

The Fed meets Sept. 15-16 with a divided set of current signals. ADP hiring weakened, Williams sees tariff effects fading and Treasury yields declined on the day. Against that, the Beige Book reported moderately faster prices, oil and refined fuels remain elevated, and Warsh has emphasized that inflation breadth is still well above its pre-pandemic norm. Payrolls, services inflation and the subsequent producer-price reports must decide whether the daily Treasury rally can become a sustained reassessment of policy.

The BOJ follows on Sept. 17-18 with a 25-basis-point increase already fully priced. Ueda’s latest comments support action, while Takata has expanded the debate to include its size and the pace of later moves. The policy statement must therefore address the path beyond September to alter expectations materially. A routine increase without guidance could leave the yen vulnerable; a more forceful signal would raise the financing pressure already reaching JGB auctions and Japanese corporate balance sheets.

Credit outcomes depend on execution rather than the benchmark-rate direction alone. Senegal must clarify the Sept. 13 coupon and the perimeter of its proposed debt treatment. Ukrenergo must complete the DFC-backed fundraising and win creditor consent on Oct. 1. Bathla’s lenders must decide which projects justify new completion capital and which collateral can support recoveries. In each case, a modest Treasury rally changes the discount rate at the margin, but not the priority, guarantee, liquidity or cash-flow questions determining creditor value.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries recover as softer hiring and Williams interrupt the global duration selloff
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries recovered modestly, led by the front end, after August private payrolls rose only 38,000 and New York Fed President John Williams challenged the assumption that oil above $90 required an immediate policy response. The 2-year yield fell 3.1 basis points to 4.37%, the 10-year eased 1.9 basis points to 4.78% and the 2s10s curve widened 1.2 basis points to 41 basis points.

The rally remained small beside the week’s selloff. The 2-year was still 15.9 basis points higher over the week, while declines in both the 10-year real yield and breakeven showed no decisive rejection of either real-rate or inflation pressure. The Beige Book also described modestly stronger activity and moderately accelerating prices, leaving the Fed to judge whether resilient investment and wages allow energy costs to spread or price-sensitive demand contains them.

Oil remained the principal counterforce as renewed US-Iran fighting kept crude, European gas and refined fuels elevated. Risk assets nevertheless treated the Treasury move as a pause in tightening rather than a flight to safety: US equities rose, volatility fell and US high-yield spreads were little changed. Tightening pressure persisted abroad as New Zealand raised rates, Canada delivered a hawkish hold, Australian growth strengthened and Japanese officials reinforced expectations of a September increase.
